title: The one-pager, the technical proposal and the internal RFC

videos.script: A decision that nobody wrote down gets made twice. Once in the meeting, and again by everybody who was not there. {{title}} This lesson is about the documents that make decisions stick. There are three sizes. {{matrix}} A one-pager asks one person for one decision, with a cost and a date. {{onepager}} A technical proposal compares a design with its alternatives, so that reviewers can find the flaw before the code does. And an RFC opens the question to everybody it affects, for a fixed time, before one named person decides. {{lifecycle}} The size of the document follows the size of the decision. How many teams it touches, and how hard it would be to undo. The last section is about the part that fails most often. Not rejection. Silence. A proposal that nobody ever decides. {{silence}}
